To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) interneurons in the O/A border of the hippocampal stratum oriens are activated by glutamate and can inhibit CA1 pyramical cells via a glutamatergic pathway, and 2) this pathway is mediated by a combination of GABA receptors.
the inhibitory synaptic potentials evoked by stimulation of interneuronal pathways in stratum ori ens of hippocampus are mediated by both GABAA and GABAB receptors.
glut‐IPSP in CA1 pyramids are mediated by both GABA‐A and GABA‐B receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the synaptic organization of the hippocampal circuitry.
the identification of the interneuron populations involved in the generation of IPSPs in CA1 pyramids and their possible contribution to the generation of the electrically induced IPSP.
the identification of the synaptic mechanisms mediating inhibitory postsynptotic potentials (IPSPs) evoked by stimulation of interneuronal networks in the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GABAergic interneurons activated by pyramidal cell stimulation in stratum pyramidalis are the only source of recurrent IPSPs, whereas interneurons activated at the oriens/alvesus border can contribute to both recurrent IPSPs (GABAA receptors) and O/A glut‐ IPSPs (mostly GABAA, but also GABAB receptors).

GABAA and GABAB receptors are involved in inhibitory synaptic potentials evoked from glutamate stimulation of O/A interneurons, but that the relative contribution of each receptor type is different depending on whether the interneurons are activated by glutamate stimulation from O/A or by electrical stimulation from PYR.
GABAA receptors mediate the majority of the inhibitory effects exerted by interneurons on pyramidal cells and that the GABAB receptors are involved in a smaller proportion of the inhibitory actions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both GABAA and GABAB receptors are involved in the inhibition of pyramidal neurons in the hippocampal CA1 region, but that GABAA receptors are the major mediators of recurrent inhibition.
the glut‐IPSP recorded in the CA1 region is mediated by both GABAA and GABAB receptors, whereas the electrically evokd IPSP is mediated by GABARs.
glutamate stimulation of O/A interneurons evokes two distinct types of IPSPs in CA1 pyramids, one mediated by GABAb receptors and the other by GABAA and GABAb receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the O/A glutamate stimulation evoked a GABA‐mediated hyperpolarization in CA1 pyramids that was sensitive to bicuculline and 2‐hydroxysaclofen, and therefore mediated by GABA(A) and GABA(B) receptors, respectively.
the GABAergic system is complex and involves many types of receptors, which are differentially distributed and have distinct functions.
the glutamate receptor type that mediates glut‐IPSP is different from that mediating recurrent inhibition, and the glut‐IPSP can be mediated by GABAb receptors.
